data.revised_prompt:
Create a polished scientific method diagram for a robotics/computer-science paper subsection titled conceptually “Closed-Loop Differentiable System”. Wide landscape figure, 1536x512, white background, crisp vector-like IEEE / Science Robotics style, elegant rounded boxes, subtle gradients, clean arrow routing, legible large typography.

Overall composition: one large central time-step block for time t, with a compact faint ghost/mini block for time t+1 on the right to indicate recurrence. Do NOT repeat three full blocks. Use a single detailed block at t and a compact repeated hint for t+1. Include a thin loop arrow from the next-state node toward the next compact block labeled “repeat”.

Left side input node: rounded node labeled exactly “x_t, c_t” with a small line below it reading “c_t=[P_t,E_t,G_t]”.

Central detailed time-step block arranged left-to-right:
1) Pale blue geometric-rendering box labeled “R(x_t,E)” with output label “D_raw,t”.
2) Larger pale cyan differentiable sensor box labeled “S_phi”. Inputs into S_phi: “D_raw,t”, “c_t”, “rho_t”, “x_t”. Outputs from S_phi: “D_obs,t”, “Q_t”, “M_t”. Include a light hatching or texture inside.
3) Pale green split-policy box labeled “Pi_theta”, containing two small sublabels inside: “Pi_f” and “Pi_c”. Inputs into Pi_theta: “D_obs,t”, “s_t”, “m_t”, “h_t”, “q_t”, “c_t”.
4) From Pi_theta branch to two outputs via small circular split nodes: output “u_t” to the dynamics module, and output “c*_{t+1}” to EMA.
5) Pale orange rounded box labeled “EMA” that computes “c_{t+1}”.
6) Pale purple rounded box labeled “f_dyn” that computes “x_{t+1}”.
7) Right next-state node labeled exactly “x_{t+1}, c_{t+1}”.
Then a faint repeated compact block or compact arrow labeled “repeat for t+1 ...” / “repeat” to show temporal iteration.

Losses below the central block:
1) Large loss box below S_phi labeled “L_sens / L_teach”, connected upward to “Q_t, M_t, c_t”.
2) Large loss box below f_dyn and Pi_theta labeled “L_flight”, connected upward to “x_{t+1}, u_t”.

Backward gradients, red arrows (curved, with arrowheads pointing backward):
- From “L_sens / L_teach” back to “S_phi” and to the left state node “c_t=[P_t,E_t,G_t]”. Label one red arrow “dL/dc_t”.
- From “L_flight” back to “f_dyn”, then to “u_t”, then to “Pi_f” inside “Pi_theta”, then to “D_obs,t”, then to “S_phi”.
- Important: Do NOT draw red gradients through “R(x_t,E)” to the environment. R is forward geometric rendering only; S_phi is the differentiable perception path.

Legend in upper-right, small but readable: “black: forward”, “red: backward”, “blue: perception”, “green: policy”, “purple: dynamics”.

Color/style guidance: black arrows for forward path; blue outline or fill for perception module; green for policy module; purple for dynamics; orange for EMA; red arrows for gradients; subtle drop shadows; clean spacing; no clutter; no 3D perspective; no dark background; no logos; no watermark; no drone icons. Make all exact labels large and legible and preserve the exact variable names.

Make the diagram elegant and expressive, with rounded boxes and clean, high-end scientific figure aesthetics. Ensure the active-depth sensor is S_phi, not R; S_phi produces D_obs, Q, M; Pi_theta contains both Pi_f and Pi_c; Pi_f outputs u_t; Pi_c outputs c*_{t+1}; EMA updates c_{t+1}; f_dyn updates x_{t+1}; two distinct losses visible; red backward gradients reach c_t through S_phi; time iteration visible through x_t,c_t -> x_{t+1},c_{t+1} -> repeat. Avoid misspellings such as S_ph or Piheta.
